claims.text:
Jim Allan recognizes the name as one of the short meaningless Hobbitish names in which case it probably represents genuine Hobbitish Sancha.
[http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Sancho Sancho] is a real Spanish name which derives from Latin sanctius "holy". This makes Sancho one of the very few Spanish names appearing in the legendarium.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix F, "On Translation"

claims.text: Jim Allan recognizes the name as one of the short meaningless Hobbitish names in which case it probably represents genuine Hobbitish Sancha.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix F, "On Translation"

claims.text: The son of Olo Proudfoot, at the age of eleven, Sancho was present at the Farewell Party of his uncle Bilbo, along with his father and grandfather Odo.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix C, "Baggins of Hobbiton"

claims.text: The day after, on 23 September, , he went to Bag End to seek for a treasure he heard rumours about. Frodo could just stop him, but not after Sancho had already started excavating the pantry, where he thought he heard an echo.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "A Long-expected Party"

claims.text: In early drafts of The Lord of the Rings, Sancho is thrown out by Frodo's (at that stage referred to as Bingo) lawyers, Iago Grubb and Folco Burrowes eject him when he tries to loot the pantry.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Return of the Shadow, "The First Phase: I. A Long-expected Party, (iii) The Third Version"
